# Joseph and Aseneth Chapter 18 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 18:2 — sons of the handmaids vs. concubines

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sons of the handmaids of Jacob" | Literal paidiskōn — female slaves/servants |
| LOGOS | "sons of Jacob's concubines" | Standard scholarly rendering |
| PNEUMA | "sons of Jacob's concubines" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS and PNEUMA agree: 'concubines.' The Greek paidiskē in this context refers to the secondary wives/concubines (Bilhah and Zilpah). 'Handmaids' (EMET) is too domestic and understates the status. Adopted LOGOS.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 18:4 — son of a slave — social insult

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the son of a slave" | Literal doulou huios |
| LOGOS | "the son of a slave" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "some slave's son" | Dismissive tone appropriate to the speaker |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** EMET and LOGOS agree: 'the son of a slave.' This is a formal statement of social hierarchy. PNEUMA's 'some slave's son' captures the contempt but is too colloquial. Adopted LOGOS.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.
